results.content: With three months to go until the U.S. midterm elections in November, voters increasingly seem to prefer Democrats over the Republican Party that has had control of Congress for the last two years. Results of a Reuters/Ipsos poll released Monday showed that 42% of registered voters would vote for a Democratic congressional candidate at present, compared to 37% for a Republican. The same survey also found that, for the first time in nearly a decade of its polling series, voters perceive the Democratic Party as having a better plan for the economy than the Republican Party. results.title: Democrats Lead Republicans in Polls Three Months Ahead of Midterms - Time Magazine

results.content: Months of immigration enforcement controversies have taken their toll, and new polling shows it could be a problem for Republicans heading into the midterms. About eight in 10 independent voters say U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has used too much force in its nationwide operations, according to a poll from YouGov, which sampled 1,000 voters in late July. An earlier YouGov poll, which was conducted before the two shootings, found that most independents – 62% – believe ICE has gone too far. results.content: ## British attitudes toward Israeli immigration have grown more negative over the past decade, with 47% now favoring fewer or no migrants from Israel. Almost half of Britons want to see fewer or no Israeli immigrants in the UK, a new YouGov poll named “Britons have a more negative view of immigration in 2026 than in 2016” has revealed. When asked, “What countries do Britons think we should allow more and fewer migrants to come from?” 23% of respondents said there should be less immigration from Israel to the UK, and 24% said there should be none.
